speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ignorant that there was a refugee crisis right here in Asia and that so many people were suffering and needed help.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Singaporeans alerted me to this crisis and many of them are sitting in the gallery here in Parliament with us this evening.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It was Chiew Tong, a student who was doing a documentary about the Rohingya refugees who first shared with me about the plight of refugees.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was more than nine years ago and I remember listening vividly to her as she spoke passionately about her school documentary project together with two other students Jade and Clarissa.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I visited them in Aceh while they were filming, and met the refugees and listened to their painful stories first-hand.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But, Sir, painful does not actually sufficiently describe the stories I have heard.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A huge part of me just cannot imagine the amount of pain the refugees must feel and the amount of suffering they have gone through.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He is Rohingya and used to live in Myanmar.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He was only eight years old when he, his 10-year-old brother and mother fled on a boat in 2015.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ayas' father had left on another boat and landed in another country earlier.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They have since lost contact and he will probably never see his father again.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a father and a son, I cannot imagine how painful it must be, to be in this situation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ayas' mother was worried that they would die if they stayed in Myanmar any longer.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And so, they too left and they spent at least three months on an overcrowded boat in the open ocean.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many lost their lives trying to flee on these boats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: According to media reports in 2015, "People were thrown overboard as the refugees fought for their survival, according to accounts of one of the grimmest episodes to emerge in a spiralling humanitarian disaster in south-east Asian waters." No one would put their children in a boat unless water was safer than land.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Despite all the dangers, it did seem for the refugees that water was ultimately safer than land.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ayas, his brother and mother finally arrived at a refugee camp in Aceh, and this is where I met him.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I met this little boy who had his childhood ripped from him, who lost his father, lost his home, who survived an arduous journey where he almost died and probably saw other people die.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I also met a little boy who was so eager to learn, who had learnt English and wanted to practise it with me, a little boy who wanted a place he can call home.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ayas is one out of hundreds of thousands of refugees all trying to find some semblance of peace.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I met many more refugees, but nothing could really prepare me for what I saw, heard and felt in the refugee camps in Bangladesh.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is suffering on a scale and to a degree that I never could have imagined.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Bangladesh government is doing their absolute best in absolutely difficult circumstances, and they too need help.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But even more than the numbers, it is the individual stories I heard that broke my heart.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I asked about the scar on the arm of a little five-year-old girl.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A child of five should not even know what a gun is, let alone being shot and hurt by one.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I saw a father weep as he spoke of watching his nine-month-old baby being stabbed to death.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I sat down to listen to a group of women who were in tears as they told me how they were raped and how they watch their husbands and babies get killed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I met a mother and her young children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They arrived at the refugee camp the same time that I arrived.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I arrived on a mini-bus, but they had walked for weeks to reach the camp.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Her husband was killed, and they hid in the forest in fear for days before walking for weeks to cross the border and find refuge in another country.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I just cannot imagine how she would explain to the little child she was carrying and an older child she was holding hands with, about what is happening.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Where is daddy and why did they have to leave their home.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And I met a young man in the prime of his life at 22 years old who is facing up to a future without his entire family: all seven were killed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He was in tears as he showed me the video of the dead bodies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A video I wished I never watched and a video I will never forget.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We cannot erase the horrors these people have faced.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But we can all do something to help to prevent their further suffering.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Singaporeans who have responded to the call for help from the refugees.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Over the past decade, I have had the privilege of working with many Singaporeans who are trying so hard to help the refugees.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This speech is dedicated to all of them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In 2016, I met Matilda, a young Singaporean who has spent the past decade speaking up, mobilising people and giving the refugees a voice here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She mobilised a group of Singaporeans to go to Aceh to help the refugees and I joined that trip.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I saw first-hand her passion, commitment and devotion towards this cause.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know it is not an easy cause to speak up for.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She said, "AFR exists in Singapore because I believe that collectively we can do more from Singapore to rally support from within, to uplift communities in our neighbouring countries." She wanted to officially register a charity, but it is close to impossible to get charity status for an non-governmental organisation (NGO) working on a foreign cause.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why make it so difficult for the younger generation to set up a cause here in Singapore and fight for what they believe in?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To register as a charity, your organisation will need to meet the conditions set out in the Charities (Registration of Charities) Regulations: "Purposes of your organisation must be beneficial wholly or substantially to the community in Singapore." I understand that we want the focus on Singapore but in the current charities landscape, we have plenty of charities focusing on the community in Singapore and I have no doubt they are here to stay.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is not a zero-sum game and we can and should have charities focusing on the communities in Singapore but also have some focusing on communities outside of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is AFR's 10th year anniversary this year – 10 years on, Matilda and AFR are still going strong.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Imagine what more they can achieve with charity status.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He was a final year law student and was trying to set up a scholarship programme for refugees.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He co-founded a society named Monolith with his friends, Brandon, Xiaodan, Mark, Adriel, Chong Wei and Cheryl.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They wanted to start a scholarship, which will cover the costs of the International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) examinations, similar to our "O" levels, for about 80 to 90 refugee students.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The typical time needed to process an FRFCP is 30 days.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Yuan Siang shared with me that he understood the need for due diligence and did his best to keep in touch with the person-in-charge.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He shared that, "We typically get a question every two to three weeks, to which we reply as quickly as we can, only to get another question two to three weeks later." He further shared, "it is hard not to get the impression that our application might be experiencing all this delay and scrutiny because we are trying to help refugees.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With each day that passes, we get more worried that rejection is inevitable." Sir, I too understand the need for due diligence but we should streamline the processes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Helping refugees, again, is incredibly difficult work, so why should we make it any harder?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In an effort to keep the regulatory burden to a minimum and ensure a business-friendly environment in Singapore, Deputy Prime Minister Gan is already overseeing a "thorough and proactive review of our rules and processes, and prune them back where possible".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is where 80% of the funds raised through a public appeal have to be applied for charitable purposes within Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The remaining 20% of funds may be for overseas charitable purposes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In Yuan Siang's case, if he did a public appeal for a scholarship for refugees, it would not make sense to use only 20% of the funds raised towards the scholarship.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Government is providing funds to help firms internationalise and build capabilities to operate overseas.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should provide the same kind of support to organisations wanting to help other countries, to do good there.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should support our local non-profit organisations who internationalise, who fly the Singapore flag proudly overseas and who lend a helping hand to our neighbours.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Let us be seen to not just venture into other countries to compete, to take, but also to give and to help.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Also, if members of the public want to donate to a foreign charitable cause, why should the Government make it difficult to do so?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should let the public, rather than the Government, decide on what and who people want to donate to.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Government should of course ensure there is due diligence and that funds collected are properly accounted for and audited.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, we should not stop or restrict Singaporeans from raising funds to help others in other countries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Despite the difficulties, he was amazing and shared with me the impact of their efforts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Singaporeans supported him and he managed to raise $59,500 and awarded 48 scholarships to mainly refugees; 65% of the students managed to score four or more As in their IGCSEs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One student shared, "Because of your generosity, I was able to fully concentrate on my studies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This scholarship instilled a sense of responsibility in me to perform better, to gain better outcomes and to ensure that the money put forward by the organisation and the donors do not go in vain.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Besides that, this scholarship has boosted my self-esteem which will benefit me immensely in the future when I am continuing my further studies." Yuan Siang hopes to continue his efforts, but he needs the support not just from fellow Singaporeans but also from the Government.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Before I end, I should stress that the Government does care about this issue and we have made progress, but as always, this housefly hopes that more can be done.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, he just met them about an hour ago.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the issue is that the scheme is scoped so narrowly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should not forget the smaller groups who do good work too.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is likely that the refugee cause that Matilda and Yuan Siang have been fighting so hard for will not be included in this scheme.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The fact that you have been able to speak in Parliament about refugees is something that has empowered ordinary people like us to believe that helping refugees is something we will find support for." I should stress that there is nothing ordinary about Yuan Siang, Brandon, Xiaodan, Mark, Adriel, Chong Wei, Cheryl, Matilda, Chiew Tong, Jade and Clarissa.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many more NGOs like Jesuit Refugee Service Singapore, Relief SG, Singapore Red Cross and many more individuals, many of whom are sitting in the gallery, that also dedicate their lives towards this important cause.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They are extraordinary Singaporeans who have chosen a difficult cause to fight for because they believe that everyone deserves a voice.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This speech is unfortunately not one filled with happy stories.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And the story of Ayas, the little boy I met at the refugee camp in Aceh, is unfortunately not a happy one as well and probably remains so.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The last I heard, he is still in a refugee camp.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He is now 18 years old and still does not have a place he can call home.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ayas, if you somehow watch this speech, know that many people continue to speak up for you here in Singapore and continue to do their best to help you.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ayas does not have a say in his future but we do.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And I sincerely hope we will support the efforts of fellow Singaporeans who are fighting so hard to help to rebuild the lives of refugees and help ensure that they too have a place they can call home and children can have a childhood that is not stolen from them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I sincerely hope that we all remember that there is no us or them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Only us – one human family, connected in ways we sometimes forget.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: His suggestions on how to encourage and facilitate their work reflect our underlying shared vision of a united people where we look out for one another and support those in need, at home or abroad.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Ng spoke about the difficulties faced by non-profit organisations (NPOs) serving foreign charitable purposes in obtaining registered charity status in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Registered charities enjoy benefits such as income and property tax exemption and therefore, there is an expectation that the resources of charities should generally be channelled back towards helping the local community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, our regulatory framework is not so rigid that we are unable to work towards being a philanthropic hub and to recognise the benefits of our local charities in doing overseas charitable work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In response to the Member's Parliamentary Question on a related topic last year, we shared that the Commissioner of Charities (COC) has granted charity status to organisations who obtained a waiver of this charity registration condition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Most of these charities are Qualifying Grantmakers who applied for charity status under the Grantmaker Scheme administered by MCCY.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Unlike typical charities, Qualifying Grantmakers are solely funded by an individual, family or institution and do not solicit for donations from the public.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Given that these Qualifying Grantmakers are privately funded, they are regulated under a lighter-touch regime, with certain regulatory requirements, such as the requirement to substantially benefit the local community, waived.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: That said, Qualifying Grantmakers are still encouraged to apply some of their funds in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The key then, is in striking a balance: a balance between allowing selected charities more flexibility to do overseas work and yet ensuring that the vast majority of our charities which are funded by donations from the public retain the focus on meeting local needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Ng also spoke about the difficulties faced by NPOs in obtaining a permit to conduct fundraising appeals for foreign charitable purposes, such as the long processing time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We appreciate the understanding shared by Mr Ng on the need for due diligence on such fundraising appeals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The permit system and checks in place today serve to maintain public trust and confidence in fundraising appeals and protect donor interests.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The COC's Office assesses the information provided by permit applicants to ensure that funds raised are used to support legitimate causes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, some applications may need longer to process as they are more complex and involve higher risks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Relevant considerations include the target amount of donations, mode of fundraising appeals, location and background of the beneficiaries, track record of the fundraisers and compliance with the past appeals, just to name a few.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Nevertheless, we understand the pressing nature of permit applications for certain types of fundraising appeals, such as for those in support of disasters or other emergencies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Hence, the COC's Office takes a risk-based approach in assessing such applications and has been expediting most of these applications.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To streamline the process of applying for foreign fundraising permits, we encourage NPOs to engage and alert us on their fundraising plans early and submit permit applications with full disclosure and complete information to facilitate each review.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Alternatively, NPOs may also choose to work with other charities or organisations that already have valid permits to support the relevant causes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: NPOs will not need to apply for a separate permit if they do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are always looking for ways to assist legitimate fundraisers in their charitable activities and welcome suggestions to improve our service delivery.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Ng also suggested that we waive the 80:20 rule for all humanitarian causes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The intent of this 80:20 rule remains relevant today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Recently, we received feedback suggesting to prohibit all local charities from conducting fundraising appeals for foreign charitable causes to focus our resources for the vulnerable in our society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I want to assure the Member that we do allow and support our charities and our organisations to raise funds for foreign charitable causes, but we are doing so in a measured manner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In 2014, the COC granted a total of 71 permits for organisations to conduct fundraising appeals for foreign charitable purposes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: [Please refer to "Clarification by Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth", Official Report, 5 February 2025, Vol 95, Issue 151, Correction By Written Statement section.] Of these, a large majority of fundraising permits had been granted the 80:20 fundraising rule waiver and this included private appeals and appeals for disaster relief efforts, such as for those affected by the Israel-Hamas conflict and other disasters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Member also expressed his hope for scope of the OHAS to be expanded.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In our previous replies to Mr Ng's past Parliamentary Questions on the OHAS, we explained the reasons for the current scope.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are glad there is strong interest in this scheme and we are confident that it would encourage more Singaporeans to help those in need overseas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Their efforts to help those in need overseas exemplify the values of compassion and generosity that our society holds dear.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This Government shares this same goal, and that is to build a more caring and inclusive society and world.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: One, whether groups that are helping refugees will be able to get charity status?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And two, I think he mentioned that when people are applying for the fundraising for foreign charitable purposes permit, some are considered as higher risk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Could he just confirm that helping refugees is considered a higher risk?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Under this lighter touch regime, the key is that most, if not all, of the funds that are actually rallied or that are mobilised are private funds.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Louis Ng, we have just about three minutes before time is up.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The groups that are helping the refugees do want to raise funds publicly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It is not just getting the money, but empowering people with the knowledge about the refugee crisis.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, they are not going to qualify for the scheme that the Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: They are hoping to get charity status, just like any other organisation and continue and be able to raise funds overseas.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: There is a second part of the question, which is the application for the fundraising for foreign charitable permit.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary had mentioned that for higher-risk causes, they will take longer time to evaluate the application.
